target_customer: Event organizers, groups and travelers booking charter buses, plus small and mid-size coach operators with spare capacity
problem: Organizing group bus travel was slow and opaque; the company let organizers book and share bus trips online using spare capacity from small coach operators.
business_model: Marketplace and software for charter and shuttle bus booking with a take on each trip

founders.name: Kyle Boulay
founders.background_notes: TechCrunch (2017-04) describes him as a web developer and designer.

founders.name: Wolf Kohlberg
founders.background_notes: TechCrunch (2017-04) says he came from booking and travel execution.

technical_complexity.rationale: A booking web app and quoting workflow over partner operators is standard marketplace engineering.

defensibility.rationale: Operator relationships and booking history help, but charter brokers could copy the web flow.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No source shows an incumbent copying or buying the company.

market_need_then: The Montreal Gazette (2016-03) profile and the company's own claims describe over 1,000 trips and 50,000 passengers by March 2016 using underused capacity of small coach operators.

branding.name_origin: Originally Sharethebus, a literal description. CEO Kyle Boulay said the old name made people think the company was only a rideshare model.
branding.domain_note: Moved to the exact match domain bus.com around 2017-04; no source gives the seller or price.

rebrands.why: The old name suggested only a rideshare model and the company wanted a more holistic positioning, per BetaKit and TechCrunch.

brand_strength.rationale: The exact category domain bus.com is a strong asset and the rebrand was covered by TechCrunch and BetaKit, but no evidence of community or virality was found.

pivots.to: Event shuttle and group transport management
pivots.why: TechCrunch headline describes event shuttle management as the focus with the Bus.com rebrand.

outcome_analysis: Bus.com raised a seed in 2015 and a Series A in April 2017 and grew to a listed team of about 90, yet the YC page now marks it inactive. No source gives a shutdown, sale or the cause, so the cause is not public and failure factors are left empty. The record shows a real raise and traction but no outcome evidence.
notes: Amount conflict: TechCrunch says $5M, BetaKit says $6.5M and Private Equity International says $6.7M for the same April 2017 Series A; the larger figures may be Canadian dollars, so TechCrunch's figure is recorded. The seed was CAD 750,000 per BetaKit, so amount_usd is null. Seedtable dates a $5M Series A to April 2016, which conflicts with the 2017 press and is not used. A $100,000 prize at Startupfest 2015 is mentioned by BetaKit and not recorded as a round. The company website fetch was rate limited and not read. Outcome searches found no shutdown report. Competitor search found only CB Insights lists with no dated source, so the list is empty.
